knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Importing Libraries

```{r libraries, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(moments)
library(naniar)
library(VIM)
library(dplyr)
library(missForest)
library(gridExtra)
```

# Importing The Dataset

```{r Importing the Dataset, echo=TRUE}

setwd("C:/Asia Pacific University/All Module Notes/Semister-3/Programming For Data Analysis/Assignment/Data Description & Data")
original_hacking_dataset <- read.csv("hackingData.csv")
summary(original_hacking_dataset)
```

## Putting the data into a frame

```{r}
raw_data_frame <- data.frame(original_hacking_dataset)

str(raw_data_frame)
```

## View the statistic of the hacking data as a whole

```{r summary of the whole data, echo=TRUE}
summary(raw_data_frame)
```

# Data Cleaning

## Checking For Missing Values in the dataset

```{r checking for missing values, echo=TRUE}
missing_values <- colSums(is.na(raw_data_frame))
missing_values
```

## Understanding Data Behaviors For Loss Column

### View Statistical Summary For Loss Column

```{r summary statistics for Loss Column, echo=TRUE}
summary(raw_data_frame$Loss)
```

### Checking the distribution of Loss

```{r}
skew_p1 <- ggplot(raw_data_frame, aes(x = Loss)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 30, fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  geom_density(color = "orange", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Loss",
       subtitle = paste("Skewness:", round(skewness(raw_data_frame$Loss, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
       x = "Loss",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
print(skew_p1)
```


### Checking number of outliers

```{r}
Q1 <- quantile(raw_data_frame$Loss, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
Q3 <- quantile(raw_data_frame$Loss, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
IQR_Value <- Q3 - Q1
IQR_outliers_before <- sum(raw_data_frame$Loss < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_Value) | raw_data_frame$Loss > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_Value), na.rm = TRUE)

cat("The Number of outliers for Loss (IQR method):", IQR_outliers_before, "\n")
```

## Visualization for outliers

```{r}
ggplot(raw_data_frame, aes(y = Loss)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Loss")
theme_minimal()
```

### Calculating percentage of missing values for Loss

```{r}
missing_Loss_percentage <- (sum(is.na(original_hacking_dataset$Loss)) / length(original_hacking_dataset$Loss)) * 100

missing_Loss_percentage
```



### Running MCAR Test

```{r MCAR Test, echo=TRUE}
mcar_test(raw_data_frame)
```



## Cleaning Loss Column

### Imputation Method using Random Forest

#### Changing Date "chr" into "Date" format

```{r}
raw_data_frame$Date <- as.Date(raw_data_frame$Date, format="%d/%m/%Y")
str(raw_data_frame)
```

### Changing Date into numeric form and inserting new column in the dataset as Date_numeric for carrying out spearman rank correlation testing.

```{r}
raw_data_frame$Date_numeric <- as.numeric(raw_data_frame$Date)
str(raw_data_frame)
```

## Checking Correlation For Using Random Forest

### Checking Correlation of Loss VS Date

```{r}
Loss_Date <- cor(raw_data_frame$Date_numeric, raw_data_frame$Loss, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
Loss_Date
```

### Checking Correlation between Loss vs Downtime

```{r}
Loss_Downtime <- cor(raw_data_frame$DownTime, raw_data_frame$Loss, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
Loss_Downtime
```

### Checking Correlation between Loss vs Ransom

```{r}
Loss_Ransom <- cor(raw_data_frame$Ransom, raw_data_frame$Loss, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
Loss_Ransom
```

### Checking Percentage of Data Missing For Ransom

```{r}
missing_values_percentage <- (sum(is.na(original_hacking_dataset$Ransom)) / length(original_hacking_dataset$Loss)) * 100
missing_values_percentage
```

### Random Forest Imputation

```{r}
data_rf <- missForest(raw_data_frame[, c("Loss", "DownTime", "Date_numeric")])
summary(data_rf$ximp$Loss)
```

### Checking error for Random Forest

```{r}
print("OOB Error Estimate:")
print(data_rf$OOBerror)
view(raw_data_frame)
```



### Putting the imputed Loss to the Original Loss data

```{r}
raw_data_frame$Loss <- data_rf$ximp$Loss
summary(raw_data_frame$Loss)
```

### Putting the imputted data into a different vector for better accessibility

```{r}
impute_data <- raw_data_frame
str(impute_data)
```

### Removing Date_numeric from imputed data as it is not needed

```{r}
impute_data$Date_numeric <- NULL
str(impute_data)
```

### Calculating numbers of outliers after imputation

```{r}
Q1 <- quantile(impute_data$Loss, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
Q3 <- quantile(impute_data$Loss, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
IQR_Value <- Q3 - Q1
IQR_outliers <- sum(impute_data$Loss < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_Value) | impute_data$Loss > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_Value), na.rm = TRUE)

cat("The Number of outliers for Loss (IQR method):", IQR_outliers, "\n")
```

### Visualization for outliers after imputation

```{r}
ggplot(impute_data, aes(y = Loss)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Loss After Imputation")
theme_minimal()
```

### Visualization of Skewness After Imputation

```{r}
p1 <- ggplot(raw_data_frame, aes(x = Loss)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 30, fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  geom_density(color = "orange", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Loss After Imputation Of Random Forest",
       subtitle = paste("Skewness:", round(skewness(raw_data_frame$Loss, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
       x = "Loss",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p1)
```

### Skewness Comparison

```{r}
data_mean <- original_hacking_dataset
data_mean$Loss[is.na(data_mean$Loss)] <- mean(data_mean$Loss, na.rm = TRUE)

data_median <- original_hacking_dataset
data_median$Loss[is.na(data_median$Loss)] <- median(data_median$Loss, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Skewness Comparison:\n",
    "1. Original data (excluding NA): ", skewness(original_hacking_dataset$Loss, na.rm = TRUE), "\n",
    "2. Mean imputation: ", skewness(data_mean$Loss), "\n", 
    "3. Median imputation: ", skewness(data_median$Loss), "\n",
    "4. After Random Forest imputation: ", skewness(data_rf$ximp$Loss), "\n")
```



# Data Transformation

## Transforming Empty Strings of Missing Rows to "NA" for every variables used according to our objective

### Data Structure Before Imputation

```{r}
summary(raw_data_frame)
view(raw_data_frame)
```

### Data Structure After Imputation

```{r}
summary(impute_data)
view(impute_data)
```

### Data Structure After Imputting "NA" values

```{r}
impute_data$Country[impute_data$Country == ""] <- "Unknown"
impute_data$OS[impute_data$OS == ""] <- NA
impute_data$WebServer[impute_data$WebServer == ""] <- NA

summary(impute_data)
view(impute_data)
```

### Reducing Loss to one decimal places

```{r}
impute_data$Loss <- round(impute_data$Loss, 1)
view(impute_data)
```



# Data Validation

## Checking Missing Values after imputation and adding "NA's"

### Missing Values For Country

```{r}
before_missing_Country <- sum(is.na(raw_data_frame$Country))
cat("Before putting NA values : ",  before_missing_Country)

after_missing_Country <- sum(is.na(impute_data$Country))
cat("\nAfter putting NA values: ", after_missing_Country)
```

### Missing Values For OS

```{r}
before_missing_OS <- sum(is.na(raw_data_frame$OS))
cat("Before putting NA values : ", before_missing_OS)

after_missing_OS <- sum(is.na(impute_data$OS))
cat("\nAfter putting NA values: ", after_missing_OS)
```

### Missing Values For Webserver

```{r}
before_missing_Webserver <- sum(is.na(raw_data_frame$WebServer))
cat("Before putting NA values : ",  before_missing)

after_missing_Webserver <- sum(is.na(impute_data$WebServer))
cat("\nAfter putting NA values: ", after_missing_Webserver)
```

### Seeing the structure of the imputed dataset

```{r}
summary(impute_data)
str(impute_data)
```

### Extracting The Dataset

```{r}
write.csv(impute_data, "hackingData.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
